top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) combine a distinct invention, the magic-wavelength lattice, with a realisation independently reproduced at the 10^-18 level in several national laboratories after about two decades. The two-name allocation maps onto proposal and realisation without omitting a co-originator, and the citation can be worded narrowly (proposal, realisation, development) to limit the priority objection from other lattice-clock groups. P001 is a close second: a mature, widely confirmed discovery, but its allocation omits Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and the 3D theorists. P003 is least mature, with an unresolved mechanism and a contested third name. A prize is still preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No documented tie to Katori or Ye, nor to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, MacDonald, Bistritzer or Jarillo-Herrero. Subject proximity as a theorist of atomic structure and precision atomic calculations may bias me toward P002; declared for the committee to weigh.
